title: Ideal gas equation and gas laws; Balanced equations and reacting masses; Concentration and standard solutions; Molar gas volume and Avogadro's law; Titrations and solution calculations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM07#t4 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM04#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM03#N.3a, AM04#N.6a, AM05#N.2, AM07#N.4a, AM08#N.6a, AM03#N.7, AM04#N.8, AM05#N.4, AM07#N.6a, AM08#N.9, AM03#N.9, AM04#N.15b.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Precipitate
items.clue: A solid formed when two solutions react, e.g. AgCl from Ag⁺ and Cl⁻.

items.label: State symbols
items.clue: The labels (s), (l), (g) and (aq) written after each species in an equation.

items.label: Pressure
items.clue: Caused by gas particles hitting the walls; it doubles when the volume is halved.

items.label: Coefficient
items.clue: A number that multiplies a whole formula and gives the ratio of amounts in moles.

questions.stem: What amount of sodium hydroxide is present in 25.0 cm³ of NaOH(aq) in which [NaOH] = 0.100 mol dm⁻³?
A gas syringe contains 2.20 cm³ of an ideal gas at 20 °C and 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa. What amount of gas does it contain? (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

Two identical sealed flasks are at the same temperature and pressure. One is filled with methane, CH₄, and the other with chlorine, Cl₂. The methane flask contains 5.00 × 10²² atoms in total. How many atoms does the chlorine flask contain? (Ar: H 1.0, C 12.0, Cl 35.5)
questions.explanation: Equal molecules: 5.00 × 10²² ÷ 5 = 1.00 × 10²² CH₄ molecules, so 1.00 × 10²² Cl₂ molecules = 2.00 × 10²² atoms.

questions.stem: Aluminium burns in oxygen to form aluminium oxide. Which equation for this reaction is correctly balanced?
questions.explanation: Al₂O₃ and O₂ are the right formulae. 3O₂ gives 6 O = 2Al₂O₃, which needs 4Al. 4 Al and 6 O each side.

questions.stem: Vinegar (ethanoic acid, a weak acid) is in the conical flask. Sodium hydroxide is added from the burette. Which indicator should be used, and what is the colour change at the end point?

options.text: Methyl orange, from red to yellow
Either indicator, because the acid and alkali react in a 1 : 1 ratio

questions.explanation: Weak acid + strong base: phenolphthalein. It is colourless in the acid and turns pink when a slight excess of alkali is present.

questions.stem: A student prepares 100.0 cm³ of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ CuSO₄(aq) by placing 3.19 g of CuSO₄(s) in a 100.0 cm³ volumetric flask, dissolving it in some distilled water, adding distilled water to the mark and mixing. The concentration is later found to be less than 0.200 mol dm⁻³. Which of the following could explain this result?

options.text: The flask still held some distilled water from rinsing when the CuSO₄ was added.
Water was added until the bottom of the meniscus was above the mark.
Half of the solution was poured into a beaker before its concentration was measured.
The CuSO₄ dissolved completely, so no solid could be seen in the flask.

questions.explanation: Overfilling makes the volume more than 100.0 while the amount stays 0.0200 mol, so c = n/V falls.

questions.stem: A volatile liquid has the empirical formula C₂H₄O. 0.200 g of it is injected into a gas syringe at 100 °C. The vapour occupies 69.7 cm³ at 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa. What is its Mr? (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
Sulfur dioxide reacts with oxygen: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g). What volume of oxygen reacts completely with 30.0 cm³ of sulfur dioxide? All volumes are measured at the same temperature and pressure.
questions.explanation: Same T and p, so volumes are in the coefficient ratio: 30.0 × 1/2 = 15.0 cm³.

questions.stem: Magnesium ribbon fizzes and dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid. Which is the ionic equation for the reaction?
questions.explanation: Cl⁻ is a spectator. 1 Mg and 2 H each side; charge 2+ each side.

questions.stem: A student records these titres: 24.30 cm³ (rough), 23.85 cm³, 23.40 cm³ and 23.50 cm³. Which mean titre should be used in the calculation?
questions.explanation: Only 23.40 and 23.50 cm³ are concordant (within 0.10 cm³). Their mean is 23.45 cm³.

questions.stem: A student adds 600.0 cm³ of water to 200.0 cm³ of 0.500 mol dm⁻³ NaCl(aq), giving 800.0 cm³ of solution. What is the concentration of NaCl in the diluted solution, in mol dm⁻³?
A hydrocarbon propellant gas is released from an aerosol can left in a hot car. 0.500 g of the gas occupies 231 cm³ at 50 °C and 1.00 × 10⁵ Pa. What is its Mr? (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
